CAPTCHAs guard sign-ups, logins, ticket sales and contact forms. When a disabled user can't get past one, they're locked out of the entire service, not just one feature.

We audited four widely used CAPTCHAs against 10 WCAG 2.2 criteria, with a focus on screen-reader users and keyboard-only users, and turned the results into a checklist for developers.

What the research shows

  • 43% of audio CAPTCHAs solved on the first try by blind participants Bigham & Cavender, 2009
  • ~51 s per audio CAPTCHA, about five times longer than sighted users on visual ones Bigham & Cavender, 2009
  • 31% of audio CAPTCHAs where three people fully agreed on the answer Bursztein et al., 2010
